request.prompt: A single RimWorld creature sprite on a transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean thin dark outline: the clodhopper, a small wingless forager from Naboo, standing on four legs. Rear view, seen from behind, drawn from the game camera about 35 degrees above the horizon. Tough, bare, ridged brown skin covers the whole body, with no feathers or plumage and fine hide texture on the back and rounded haunches. Two hind legs are planted beneath the haunches, with a short stub of tail between them, and the large, powerful clawed forelegs, heavier than any bird's limbs, stand sturdy and planted at both flanks. The crimson neck dips forward and shows only as a tip above the shoulders; the head, with its pale beak, is carried low and forward and is hidden by the body, so eyes and beak are out of sight. All four legs are visible beneath the body. The animal fills the canvas at the same body size as its south and east views, in the same palette, brushwork and outline weight, so the three facings read as one commissioned painting of one animal. Reference: the accepted south and east views of this clodhopper.
